problem_name: Persistent yield gap and stagnant paddy productivity
problem_definition: National average paddy yields have stayed between about 2.4 and 3.1 t/ha since 2000, far below neighbours and below simulated attainable yields.

immediate_causes: Poor water control and stress-prone environments (flood, drought, salinity)
Shift to broadcast direct seeding under labor scarcity
root_causes: Weak public investment in research and extension

evidence.claim: USDA PSD national rough-rice yield ranged 2.43-3.10 t/ha over 2000-2025 (3.10 in 2000, 2.71 in 2024); Vietnam reported 6.12 t/ha in 2024.
Exploitable rice yield gaps are relatively large in Myanmar compared with Indonesia and Vietnam; the regional average gap is 48% of yield potential.
Monsoon yields in Taikkyi (Yangon) varied 0.8-4.1 t/ha, mean 2.6 t/ha (100 households, 2010).
ORYZA-simulated climatic yield potential ranged from 5.4 t/ha upward at dry-zone and delta sites, far above farmers' yields.
Ayeyarwady rice growers (n=300) showed mean technical, allocative and economic efficiency of 76.1%, 47.9% and 34.2%.
Yields rose 16.3% from 2010 to 2020 but fell 4.9% between 2020 and 2022.
National monsoon yields on farmers' largest plots fell 8% in 2025 versus 2023.
The widening yield gap with Vietnam is attributed more to differences in public investment in technology than to price policy.

geographic_scope: National; largest absolute gaps in Delta and Coastal zones; Kayah and Chin lowest yields (conflict).
farmers_affected: Most rice farmers nationally (MAPS samples 2,700-3,100 producers per monsoon round represent all states/regions).
yield_impact: Gap to attainable yield is multiple t/ha in favourable areas (S114, S189).
financial_impact: Lower yields combined with rising costs drove 2025 profits to a six-year low (S302).
data_availability: National series (D01, D02) and plot-level panel yields (D04) are available; official subnational yields not public after 2020 (S251).
data_science_potential: Yield-gap decomposition, efficiency analysis, and targeting of yield constraints by agro-ecological zone using MAPS panel.
title: Persistent yield gap and stagnant paddy productivity

problem_name: Cost-price squeeze: rising input costs, falling farm profitability
problem_definition: Input, labour and mechanization costs have risen much faster than farmgate paddy prices, pushing paddy profits to multi-year lows.

causal_chain.symptom: Falling profit per acre; reduced input use
immediate_causes: Higher wages, mechanization fees, fertilizer and fuel prices
Lower farmgate paddy prices tracking world prices
root_causes: Dual exchange-rate regime and import restrictions

evidence.claim: Between the 2023 and 2025 monsoons: urea +23%, plowing costs +55%, wages +88% (men) and +83% (women), input expenditure per acre +63%, farmgate paddy -6%, nominal profit per acre -40% (lowest in six years).
Real paddy profits in the 2024 dry season fell 15% versus 2023 after a 41% rise the year before - profitability is volatile.
The dual exchange-rate system acted as an across-the-board export tax of about 24% (Aug 2022-Aug 2024) and raised fertilizer prices ~10% relative to Thailand.
By end-June 2026 diesel was 34% and petrol 57% higher than end-February; urea reference prices were 28-49% above the previous monsoon.

geographic_scope: National; insecure areas face higher input costs (+1-6%).
farmers_affected: National paddy producers (MAPS: 2,734 producers in 2025 monsoon round).
data_availability: MAPS farm budgets each season (D04); monthly retail prices (D06, D24, D35); exchange-rate estimates (D36).
data_science_potential: Season-ahead profitability nowcasts, input-price pass-through models, price-aware input recommendations.
title: Cost-price squeeze: rising input costs, falling farm profitability

problem_name: Rural labour scarcity and rising agricultural wages
problem_definition: Out-migration and conflict have tightened rural labour markets, raising wages and changing how rice is established and harvested.

causal_chain.symptom: Higher wage bill; labour unavailable at peak operations

evidence.claim: Since 2011 farmers faced labour shortages and rising wages as workers moved to urban sectors; they responded by mechanizing rapidly.
Farm wages rose 88% (men) and 83% (women) between the 2023 and 2025 monsoons.
Farmers in the most insecure areas were 7-15 percentage points more likely to report lacking access to agricultural labourers.
Labour shortages and water constraints are the primary reasons for adopting direct-seeded rice.
Women perform 39% of household farm labour days and are 43% of agricultural wage workers.
Combine harvester use releases family labour into more remunerative dry-season non-farm employment.

yield_impact: Indirect via broadcasting and delayed operations (S302).
financial_impact: Wage bill is the fastest-rising cost (S302).
data_availability: Wages in MAPS (D04); migration in MHWS and Migration Assessment (D05, D30); wage measurement bias studied (S297).
data_science_potential: Township wage nowcasting, labour-saving technology targeting, panel analysis of migration and mechanization.
title: Rural labour scarcity and rising agricultural wages

problem_name: Fertilizer cost, access and declining use efficiency
problem_definition: Fertilizer is farmers' most important commercial input; conflict and FX distortions raised prices, cut use and lowered yield response per unit of nitrogen.

causal_chain.symptom: Lower or mistimed fertilizer use; weak yield response
immediate_causes: High urea prices relative to paddy
Reduced access to extension and optimal blends
root_causes: Absence of site- and price-specific recommendations

evidence.claim: Greater intensity of violent events is associated with higher fertilizer prices (especially far from import points), lower use, lower rice yield response at given N, and a decline in fertilizer use efficiency each year since the conflict began.
Monsoon fertilizer use fell about 20% across 2020-2022 monsoons.
In the 2022 dry season fertilizer use fell only 6% despite a 51% price increase.
Fertilizer use on rice rose 20% in the 2023 monsoon as urea prices fell 16%, contributing to a 7% yield gain.
In 2025, doubling chemical fertilizer use was associated with a 9% higher yield, and doubling commercial input spending with 34% higher yield (ceteris paribus, correlational).
Surveyed rice farmers in central Myanmar (n=600) applied more fertilizer than previously reported national averages, but timing departed from recommended practices.

geographic_scope: National; highest prices in remote/conflict areas.
data_availability: Plot-level fertilizer quantities, prices and yields in MAPS (D04); soil data coarse (D17); no public nutrient-omission trial database identified.
data_science_potential: Economic-optimum N by zone and price ratio; yield-response estimation with panel controls; advisory delivery and A/B evaluation.
title: Fertilizer cost, access and declining use efficiency

problem_name: Flood, cyclone and heavy-rain losses in Delta and coastal rice
problem_definition: Monsoon floods, heavy rain and cyclones repeatedly cut paddy yields in low-lying Delta and coastal townships.

causal_chain.symptom: Seasonal yield losses and crop failure

evidence.claim: In the 2025 monsoon, 10% of paddy farmers reported floods (yields -34% when affected) and 15% heavy rains (-15%).
In the 2023 monsoon floods affected 7% of farmers with 32% yield losses.
Cyclone Mocha affected 13% of crop farmers; 3% lost their whole dry-season harvest; coastal yields fell 29%.
Of 1,046 cyclone events (1970-2018) in four countries, 138 were associated with recorded rice damage; agricultural losses are under-reported in disaster databases.
Tropical cyclone track hot spots along Myanmar's coast changed over 1983-2012.

geographic_scope: Ayeyarwady, Bago, Yangon, Rakhine, Mon, Tanintharyi
farmers_affected: 7-15% of paddy farmers per monsoon report flood/heavy rain shocks (S252, S302).
data_availability: Open SAR flood mapping (D09, D16, D26), rainfall (D13, D15), cyclone tracks (D21), farmer-reported shocks with township (D04).
data_science_potential: Township flood-exposure index, loss estimation, anticipatory targeting, index-insurance basis-risk analysis.
title: Flood, cyclone and heavy-rain losses in Delta and coastal rice

problem_name: Drought and rainfall variability in the Central Dry Zone
problem_definition: Erratic rainfall and dry spells limit rainfed and pump-irrigated rice in the semi-arid Central Dry Zone.

evidence.claim: Drought-affected farmers (5%) saw 51% lower paddy yields in the 2023 monsoon.
MODIS NDVI and CHIRPS rainfall are strongly correlated in the Dry Zone (R2 0.74 and 0.82), supporting satellite drought monitoring.
The Central Dry Zone hosts ~12 million people and 35% of Myanmar's grain cropping but is food-insecure.
Erratic rainfall, dry spells and untimely rain were the critical challenge in rice-based farming; timely machinery use was a major adaptation.

data_availability: CHIRPS, IMERG, ERA5-Land, MODIS (open); MAPS shocks.
data_science_potential: Drought early warning (SPI/NDVI anomalies), seasonal planting advisories.
title: Drought and rainfall variability in the Central Dry Zone

problem_definition: Dry-season saline intrusion prevents summer rice near the coast and depresses yields and variety choice.

causal_chain.symptom: No summer rice / low coastal yields
immediate_causes: Saline river water in dry season

evidence.claim: Summer rice cannot be grown near the Ayeyarwady coast because river water salinity is high in the dry season; Sentinel-2 visible reflectance correlates with electrical conductivity.
Past exposure to saltwater intrusion reduced adoption of high-value varieties in coastal townships (298 households).
Coastal agro-ecological zone yields fell 22% in the 2025 monsoon versus 2023, the largest decline of any zone (partly due to Rakhine market isolation).
Delta land elevation datasets differ substantially, affecting sea-level-rise exposure estimates.

geographic_scope: Coastal Ayeyarwady (Labutta, Bogale, Pyapon, Mawlamyinegyun), Rakhine
trend: Likely worsening with sea-level rise (not quantified in corpus)
data_availability: Sentinel-2 open; in-situ EC measurements scarce (must be collected).
data_science_potential: Salinity mapping model operationalisation; dry-season planting-window advisory.
title: Salinity intrusion in coastal Delta

problem_name: Conflict and macro-policy shocks disrupting production and markets (post-2021)
problem_definition: Violence after the 2021 coup, plus FX controls, reduced productivity, technology use, credit and market access.

causal_chain.symptom: Lower productivity and market participation in insecure areas
immediate_causes: Reduced extension, inputs, credit and labour access
root_causes: Dual exchange rate and trade restrictions

evidence.claim: Increases in fatal violent events (2020-2021) reduced rice total factor productivity by ~4% on average in the short run; poorer, less-capitalised farmers were more affected.
Conflict reduced paddy production, yield, farmgate prices and value of production; events targeting civilians had larger effects.
Formal agricultural credit declined sharply in conflict areas while informal credit stayed resilient.
Rice distribution costs rose 31% (monsoon) and 146% (dry season), partly linked to conflict.
Rakhine State was largely cut off from commercial input and output markets in 2025.

geographic_scope: National; most severe in Sagaing, Kayah, Chin, Rakhine and parts of Magway/Mandalay (per sources).
financial_impact: Lower farmgate prices in conflict areas (S228)
data_availability: ACLED (D18) + MAPS (D04) panel; data collection in conflict zones has measurable but modest bias (S297).
data_science_potential: Conflict-aware targeting of input/advisory support; spatial econometrics.
title: Conflict and macro-policy shocks disrupting production and markets (post-2021)

problem_name: Weak and shock-sensitive access to quality seed
problem_definition: Farmers increasingly recycle own seed; off-farm quality seed access falls after weather and conflict shocks.

evidence.claim: Using off-farm seed is associated with higher monsoon yields; off-farm seed use declined in 2021-2023 and fell after rainfall, temperature, flood and violence shocks, but less so in townships hosting EGS seed or research farms.
Use of self-preserved seed rose 17 percentage points compared with 2020.
Improved varieties benefit farmers only if adopted; demand for quality seed in the Dry Zone is constrained.

geographic_scope: National; Delta and Dry Zone analysed
yield_impact: Positive yield association of off-farm seed (S299)
data_availability: MAPS seed source (D04); seed farm locations from secondary sources (S299) - not a public dataset.
data_science_potential: Seed-access gap mapping; location of seed multiplication.
title: Weak and shock-sensitive access to quality seed

problem_definition: Large irrigation schemes and pump schemes deliver less water and fewer dry-season crops than designed.

evidence.claim: Of ~12 million ha cropped in 2014, about 7 million ha were rice; irrigation expansion potential was assessed.
Water users' associations in pump schemes enabled farmers to double irrigated area 1.5 years after the project ended (self-reported).
MODIS VI time series identified a canal with limited water supply inside the Thapanzeik irrigation district (2001-2020).
A dam in Yedashe enabled double rice cropping and higher incomes (95-farmer before/after comparison).

geographic_scope: Dry Zone schemes and Delta polders
data_availability: Satellite VI and water (D12, D16); scheme records not public.
data_science_potential: Remote-sensing performance benchmarking of irrigation command areas.
title: Irrigation and water-control underperformance

problem_name: Harvest and post-harvest losses (drying, storage, rodents)
problem_definition: Traditional harvesting, field stacking, sun drying and storage cause quantity and quality losses.

evidence.claim: In an Ayeyarwady field experiment, mechanized practices raised net income 30-50% versus traditional practice and significantly reduced post-harvest losses without raising life-cycle GHG.
Rodent losses in granaries ranged 1.2-14% across two townships and two years.
Reversible-airflow flatbed dryers were the best option on cost-benefit, labour and energy across four countries including Myanmar.

data_availability: No national loss dataset; experimental data only.
data_science_potential: Dryer/mill location-allocation; loss-risk mapping using harvest-time rainfall.
title: Harvest and post-harvest losses (drying, storage, rodents)

problem_name: Mechanization service access and rising service costs
problem_definition: Rapid, market-driven mechanization through outsourcing is now threatened by fuel prices, conflict and rising fees.

causal_chain.symptom: Falling combine use; higher plowing fees

evidence.claim: Extremely rapid mechanization occurred 2011-2020; land preparation, harvesting and threshing became near scale-neutral via outsourcing markets.
Over about ten years, tractor plowing rose 43 pp and combine harvesting 41 pp.
Combine use on rice in the 2023 monsoon was 12 pp lower than in 2020; mechanization costs rose 42% (2022-2023) and 55% (2023-2025).
Small rice plots were ~30% more productive than large ones; rising mechanization fees attenuated this inverse relationship, more so in conflict-affected townships.

data_availability: MAPS mechanization use and fees; service-provider surveys (D32).
data_science_potential: Service coverage gaps mapping; fee monitoring; routing/scheduling of combine services.
title: Mechanization service access and rising service costs

problem_definition: Government and microfinance credit fell after 2021; farmers withdraw from credit markets and self-finance.

immediate_causes: Collapse of formal lending in conflict areas

evidence.claim: Formal credit receipt declined sharply in conflict areas, especially from government schemes and MFIs; informal credit (family, agribusiness) remained resilient.
A large subsidised rice credit programme showed little evidence of raising yields or output but some positive effect on household income (fuzzy RDD).
Credit-labour interlinked transactions persist in the Delta because subsistence needs dominate.

data_availability: MAPS credit modules; MADB data not public.
data_science_potential: Limited - credit is a policy/institutional problem.
title: Contraction of formal agricultural credit

problem_name: Extension and information gap (research does not reach farmers)
problem_definition: Public extension weakened, and proven decision tools (e.g., Rice Crop Manager) did not scale; digital channels are emerging.

causal_chain.symptom: Farmers use generic or outdated practices

evidence.claim: Conflict reduced farmers' access to extension, which otherwise helps maintain productivity with limited capital.
A Rice Crop Manager prototype for Myanmar was developed and shared with the Department of Agriculture in 2019; no evidence of scale-up was found.
A private digital climate-advisory platform scaled to 139,000 farmers (10 commodities) in 2025.
An RCT in post-coup Myanmar evaluated direct SMS vs lead-farmer-supported SMS extension for fall armyworm management.

data_availability: Advisory-usage data held by platforms; MAPS extension module.
data_science_potential: Personalised advisory content, A/B testing, uptake analytics.
title: Extension and information gap (research does not reach farmers)

problem_name: Price distortions and weak price transmission (FX, export policy)
problem_definition: Exchange-rate controls and trade policy reduce farmgate incentives; domestic/export price links shift with policy.

causal_chain.symptom: Low farmgate prices relative to export parity

evidence.claim: Exchange-rate policies were much more harmful to farm incentives than domestic trade effects of insecurity.
Myanmar became the world's 5th-largest rice exporter by end-2019; exports proved resilient during the crisis years.
Rice markets showed partial integration under a halfway-liberalised system (co-integration and VAR analysis).

data_availability: Monthly prices (D06, D24, D35), exchange rates (D36), trade (D23).
title: Price distortions and weak price transmission (FX, export policy)

problem_name: Agricultural statistics and monitoring data gaps
problem_definition: Official subnational production data are not publicly available after 2020, and key price and loss datasets have coverage holes.

causal_chain.symptom: Decisions made without current subnational evidence
immediate_causes: Price monitoring gaps in main rice regions

evidence.claim: Agricultural production data were publicly available at regional scale only for 2012-2020.
WFP's Myanmar retail rice price records (2008-2026; 298 markets report low-quality rice) contain no markets in Ayeyarwady, Bago (West) or Nay Pyi Taw - including the main rice basket (Ayeyarwady).
evidence.note: Derived by this project from the HDX file downloaded 2026-10-09.

evidence.claim: Recall bias in reported wages is modest and does not increase with conflict severity.
Agriculture-related cyclone damage is under-reported in major multi-peril disaster databases.

trend: Partially filled by phone surveys (MAPS, MHWS) and satellites
data_availability: Open satellite archives; MAPS/MHWS phone panels.
title: Agricultural statistics and monitoring data gaps

problem_definition: Biotic stresses are the most frequently reported production shock.

evidence.claim: Pests, diseases and weeds were the most frequent shock in the 2023 monsoon (13% of farmers).
Asynchronous planting after Cyclone Nargis extended rodent breeding, followed by an outbreak 15 months later.
Weed infestation reduced the productivity of hybrid and inbred rice.

data_availability: Farmer-reported shocks (D04); no pest surveillance data public.
data_science_potential: Image-based detection exists in prototypes (S279, S293); surveillance data are the binding constraint.
title: Pests, diseases, weeds and rodents

problem_name: Shift to broadcast direct seeding and its yield trade-off
problem_definition: Labour and water constraints push farmers to broadcast direct seeding, which farmers perceive as lower-yielding.

evidence.claim: Direct-seeded rice is used by ~50% of farmers in the monsoon and ~75% in the dry season, mostly by broadcasting; farmers perceive a transplanting yield advantage of ~11 baskets per acre.
Lower 2025 productivity was associated with reduced labour inputs and more broadcasting.
Direct seeding rose ~20 pp over about a decade.

data_availability: Establishment method, wages and yields in MAPS (D04).
data_science_potential: Establishment-method profitability model by zone and wage level; row/drum-seeder service targeting.
title: Shift to broadcast direct seeding and its yield trade-off

problem_definition: Continuous flooding and residue burning contribute GHG; mitigation evidence is experimental only.

evidence.claim: Field experiments compared AWD with continuous flooding and manure levels for GHG and water productivity.
Mechanized post-harvest did not increase life-cycle GHG emissions.

title: Environmental footprint of paddy (methane, energy)
